before_snapshot.comment:
APPROVED Li-O2 HIERARCHICAL ENGINEERING RECONCILIATION, item18, 2026-10-18. Wang,Deng,Yuan2020 DOI10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.121339, SI TablesS3/S4/S5/S16; Kanthal resistance-wire datasheet https://www.kanthal.com/products/datasheets/material-datasheets/wire/resistance-heating-wire-and-resistance-wire/nikrothal-80/. Adopt TableS3 detailed retained geometry: cell182.6kg, module hardware19.51, pack hardware43.67, oxygen tank55, BMS4,cooling29.07 =>333.85kg at63.5grosskWh. This conflicts with source headline321kg/267kg pack and with TableS5 gross material figures; do not mix those bases. Scalable cell/module/pack hardware=245.78kg; fixed-per-reference auxiliary hardware=88.07kg. Listed component masses, not proportional normalization of contradictory gross LCI tables, define this engineering reference. Known cell ingredients total182.59kg;0.01kg unspecified cathode catalyst remains a documented composition gap, not zero-metal proof. The sourceS4 fluoropolymer binder is not substituted for the unidentified S3 catalyst; binder quantity/fate is also unresolved, and that old process input is disabled in this reference. Electrolyte total59.11kg is split by inheritedS4 salt:solvent ratio.016:.308; LiClO4 process is the inherited salt provider, and ethylene-glycol dimethyl ether remains an explicitly imperfect TEGDME solvent proxy. Lithium protective film/pouch/separator process recipes remain inherited and unvalidated. Collector feed is1kg metal/kg foil at100percent reference retention; matching rolling and restored facility proxy are preserved. Terminal metal fractions are2.44kgAl/10.5kg and8.06kgCu/10.5kg, with matching working services; old overlapping gross feed and implied manufacturing scrap are disabled under the explicit100percent retention reference. Module and pack known material inputs followS3, with no new gross-yield claim. Module monitor.67kg is counted once; BMS4kg is assigned to central protection only using4/4.518 of the separate engineering central-control package. This functional repartition is an assumption, not a source breakdown. Cooling uses7kg Al plus22.07kg pureEG reference (alternative50/50 coolant is a sensitivity); thermal duty, pump/hoses remain gaps. Heater.2kg uses an idealized binary80Ni/20Cr resistance-alloy reference, consistent with a NiCr class but not a complete measured battery heater/Nikrothal composition; electronic/heater construction is unresolved. Preserve historical source-specific S16 recycling coefficients without new recovery credits. Capacity purchases245.78/63.5kg scalable hardware plus one auxiliary lifecycle unit per63.5kWh. Its negative waste equals scalable mass; auxiliary unit carries its own88.07kg waste. Future density factors scale hardware and its waste together; fixed auxiliary manufacture/treatment stay paired. Existing relative density learning is retained as an engineering ratio; absolute cell energy63.5/182.6=.347754655kWh/kg and fixed recipe are not a validated future design. Original full-battery market remains manufacturing-only at333.85kg component-sum basis; capacity uses the separately named hardware market. Vehicle energy/lifetime allocation is unchanged. Source contradictions, catalyst, solvent, future structure and recovery performance remain explicit gaps.
PREVIOUS NOTES (retained as history; the correction above takes precedence):
APPROVED Li-O2 SINGLE RECYCLING BOUNDARY, 2026-10-18. Wang, Deng and Yuan (2020), DOI 10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.121339, supporting information Table S16, explicitly describes recycling per 1 kg Li-O2 battery system. Its six treatment coefficients are retained. Set the former -1/321 kg/kg internal treatment fragment to a deterministic zero and apply end of life only at market for battery capacity, Li-ion, Li-O2: the full purchased battery mass is sent to treatment of LiO2 battery, for recycling (RER; waste LiO2 battery). Standalone manufacture is manufacturing-only. DefaultInventory may retain the zero exchange; it contributes no treatment flow. Do not add a second generic Li-ion route. This restores a single historical source-specific accounting route; treatment yields, whole-system mass normalization, modern recovery and primary/secondary shares remain unvalidated. No new recovery credit or change to manufacturing recipes, density or lifetime.
PREVIOUS NOTES (retained as history; the correction above takes precedence):
System: 63.5kWh Li-O2 || Mass (excl. O2 tanks): 267 kg || Battery energy density: 238 Wh/kg || System energy density (incl. O2 tanks): 198 Wh/kg || Battery lifetime: 305 kWh/kg (1.76 MJ/km x 2e5 km / 321 kg). Source: Originally from Wang, F., Deng, Y., & Yuan, C. (2020). Life cycle assessment of lithium oxygen battery for electric vehicles. Journal of Cleaner Production, 264, 121339. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.121339
